items.title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Read only a group's own regions in hybrid SSM transfers
items.author: NickLucche
items.summary: In hybrid MLA+SSM models, the NIXL hybrid descriptor path made every attention group read all registered regions. Some regions hold only SSM-layer pages or only scratch pages, so each MLA block also re-read bytes owned by other groups.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

In hybrid MLA+SSM models, the NIXL hybrid descriptor path made every attention group read **all** registered regions. Some regions hold only SSM-layer pages or only scratch (`CircularBufferSpec`) pages, so each MLA block also re-read bytes owned by other groups. On GLM-5.3-Flash, about 38% of the bytes on the wire were duplicates. This PR records, per transfer group, which regions hold its layers and addresses only those.

items.title: [Perf] mooncake: Reduce KV transfer descriptor construction overhead
items.author: SouthWest7
items.summary: Mooncake's generic KV transfer path splits paired page indices into Python lists, builds a tuple for every layer and contiguous run, then unpacks those tuples into the three lists consumed by. Fragmented page maps make this CPU work grow with the number of tra…
items.body:
## Motivation

Mooncake's generic KV transfer path splits paired page indices into Python lists, builds a `(src, dst, length)` tuple for every layer and contiguous run, then unpacks those tuples into the three lists consumed by `batch_transfer_sync`. Fragmented page maps make this CPU work grow with the number of transfer descriptors.

Build the descriptor columns directly to reduce preparation overhead. Related to the PD transfer-efficiency work in #43699.

## Modifications

- Represent contiguous runs by their source start, destination start, and length, without materializing each page list.

items.title: [Bug] NGRAM speculative decoding corrupts radix-cached KV with the overlap scheduler when requests end on a stop token (0.5.22)
items.author: DiaaAj

items.body:
## Summary
With `speculative_algorithm="NGRAM"` and otherwise default settings, greedy (temperature 0) outputs of a
few concurrent requests are wrong. The radix cache, overlap scheduler and CUDA graphs are all on by
default; on 0.5.21, disabling any one of them made the outputs exact, and on 0.5.22 disabling the overlap
scheduler does. The trigger is requests that share prefixes, in a workload where requests end on a stop
token. Greedy speculative decoding should be lossless, so
this is silent corruption.

- **History:** in 0.5.21 it also showed with `ignore_eos` and `max_new_tokens` endings.

items.summary: Sparse-prefill scratch replacement allocates its new tensor while the backend still owns the old one. A larger workspace (or a different dtype) can therefore fail even when the replacement alone fits the available allocator budget.
items.body:

Sparse-prefill scratch replacement allocates its new tensor while the backend still owns the old one. A larger workspace (or a different dtype) can therefore fail even when the replacement alone fits the available allocator budget.

items.author: kimseunghyun-kr
items.summary: A torchcodec wheel built for another CUDA version raises at import, and vLLM's torchcodec import guards catch only and. Every then stops at import, also for text-only models, because imports.
items.body:
## Overview

A torchcodec wheel built for another CUDA version raises `OSError` at import, and vLLM's torchcodec import guards catch only `ImportError` and `RuntimeError`. Every `vllm serve` then stops at import, also for text-only models, because `vllm.v1.core.sched.output` imports `vllm.multimodal`. This PR treats that `OSError` as "torchcodec is not available", as vLLM already does for a missing FFmpeg.

## Claims

- `vllm serve` no longer stops at import when torchcodec is installed but its native library cannot load (for example a torchcodec built for CUDA 13 in a CUDA 12.9 environment)

## Overview

## Claims

- A tool call cut by `max_tokens` no longer appears in `content`: DSML in content goes from 22/88 to 0/88 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

items.summary: CPython only appends in place to a local variable, so on an attribute every token copies the whole output text, and per-step frontend CPU grows linearly with output length (quadratic per request). This keeps the text as a rarely copied head plus a short tail.
items.body:
## Overview

`BaseIncrementalDetokenizer.update` does `self.output_text += piece` per token. CPython only appends in place to a local variable, so on an attribute every token copies the whole output text, and per-step frontend CPU grows linearly with output length (quadratic per request). This keeps the text as a rarely copied head plus a short tail. Same goal as the draft #36023, whose author [doesn't plan to finish it](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36023#issuecomment-6246472478) (the Rust frontend avoided the problem for them); the Rust frontend is opt-in (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTE

```text
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

This occurs because the core engine orchestrates separate background pr

## Overview

items.author: samridh10exe
items.summary: With, Kimi-K3 prefill returns NaN after about 1,800 tokens. Triton is correct on the same inputs.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #44758. With `--linear-attn-prefill-backend nvidia_kda`, Kimi-K3 prefill returns NaN after about 1,800 tokens. Triton is correct on the same inputs.

The A_kk inverse kernel inverted each 16x16 diagonal block with a power series on bf16 operands. When beta is close to 1 and the keys are similar, the terms of the series get large and bf16 loses the result. The inverse was wrong in every chunk, so the recurrent state grew each chunk until it overflowed. Against an fp64 reference, every stage before the inverse matches.

## Modifications

- Invert the diagonal blocks by forwa

items.author: Juntian777
items.summary: Fixes DecodeBenchConnector to report all transfer groups (including bounded-replay sliding-window groups) as loaded, preventing unnecessary prefix replays that corrupt decode-only benchmarks.
items.body:
## Purpose

`DecodeBenchConnector` fills a new request's own blocks in every KV cache group, like a P/D transfer, but it inherits the base `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids`, which reports only the prefix-cacheable groups (what a hash-addressed store holds). A bounded-replay sliding-window group (DeepSeek V4.1) is not prefix-cacheable, so the scheduler treats the window as not loaded and replays it on the first step of every filled request. ## Purpose

Since #56560, `EmulationMxfp8LinearKernel` dequantizes MXFP8 weights to BF16 once at load time, but `apply_weights` still calls `F.linear` directly. That skips the platform's unquantized-GEMM dispatch, which a BF16 checkpoint of the same layer would use.

On ROCm, that dispatch (`rocm_unquantized_gemm`) picks the skinny wvSplitK / LLMM1 kernels at decode batch sizes, while `F.linear` runs the 1-row GEMM on large hipBLASLt tiles. ## What

`TorchSampling.filter_logits` ran `last_token_logits.div_(temperature)` in
the input's dtype. For BF16/FP16 logits that

    at moderate temperatures like 0.1, and

    `MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=1e-6` → `logits * 1e6` → `inf`).

the dynamic engine: BF16 rounding changes which token wins at temperature=0.1,
top_p=0.9; FP16 scaling overflows at temperature=0.

When a LoRA slot is reused, `load_lora_weight_to_buffer` only zeroes the `embed_tokens` / `lm_head` buffers for adapters that have no embedding weights at all. The next request then runs with another adapter's weights and nothing complains.

It needs `--max-loras-per-batch` smaller than the number of adapters in use, so slots actually get reused, plus adapters that carry embedding / `lm_head` LoRA weights.

#57435 folded the inverse RoPE into the split-K sparse decode reduce, and `rocm_sparse_attn_decode` now returns how many rows it already rotated so `forward_mqa` can skip them. But only gfx942/gfx950 run that split-K reduce. Every other arch takes the fallback kernel, which never applies the inverse RoPE, yet the function still reports every row as rotated. Those rows never get rotated.

This PR reports rotated row

items.title: [Fix] speculative: Count proposals from completed adaptive rounds
items.author: riversky0014
items.summary: Adaptive speculative decoding can change its verify width while a request is running. Request metadata currently multiplies the verify count by the startup width, and log metrics multiply by the current width.

Adaptive speculative decoding can change its verify width while a request is running. For example, 127 zero-proposal rounds can be reported as 254 proposed drafts when startup uses two draft steps.

items.title: [Fix] disaggregation: Preserve EAGLE/MTP draft KV during CPU retraction
items.author: tanth47
items.summary: Related to #39749, which fixes full DFlash draft KV but explicitly leaves EAGLE/MTP unregistered. PD decode retraction with saves the target allocator's KV, but separate EAGLE/MTP pools use the same token slots without being included in that backup.
items.body:
## Motivation

Related to #39749, which fixes full DFlash draft KV but explicitly leaves EAGLE/MTP unregistered.

PD decode retraction with `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup cpu_tensor` saves the target allocator's KV, but separate EAGLE/MTP pools use the same token slots without being included in that backup. Reusing those slots overwrites draft history before the request resumes. For GLM DSA this includes draft index keys/scales as well as MLA KV.

#34801 covers the host-pool path. It does not fix CPU-tensor backups; #36343 deliberately keeps CPU tensors as the implicit ROCm fallbac

items.title: [Frontend] Accept images on /v1/systemone for multimodal next-token models
items.author: Vigilans
items.summary: rejects for models read through, such as Qwen3.5, with, although already places images ahead of the state since #60676. The strategy declares no media, so refuses the request before the read. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

`/v1/systemone` rejects `images` for models read through `NextTokenStrategy`, such as Qwen3.5, with `this model does not take image inputs`, although `NextTokenStrategy.read()` already places images ahead of the state since #60676. The strategy declares no media, so `ServingStructuredDecisions._media()` refuses the request before the read. This makes `NextTokenStrategy` accept images when the loaded model takes multimodal inputs.

No open PR changes the media `NextTokenStrategy` accepts: #60745 adds image inputs to `/v1/decisions`, and #61192, #61216 and #61251 change other part

items.title: [Feat] PD: Add opt-in first-chunk decode KV allocation
items.author: sufubao
items.summary: Decode-side allocation can reserve KV capacity while prefill is still computing. avoids that reservation but delays KV transfer until prefill finishes.
items.body:
## Motivation

Decode-side `early` allocation can reserve KV capacity while prefill is still computing. `prefill_complete` avoids that reservation but delays KV transfer until prefill finishes.

Add an opt-in `first_chunk` policy: **the first accepted prefill chunk triggers one full-request destination reservation**, allowing KV transfer to overlap the remaining prefill. This reduces the time that decode KV is reserved before it can receive data.

Enable on **both P and D**:

```bash
--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy first_chunk
```

The default remains `early`. This changes allocation

items.author: Jzz1943
items.summary: Enable decode-side prefix KV reuse for hybrid attention models in PD serving, including linear EAGLE/MTP. Requests with a shared prefix can reuse its KV on the decode worker instead of allocating and transferring another copy for every request.

## Motivation

Enable decode-side prefix KV reuse for hybrid attention models in PD serving, including linear EAGLE/MTP. Requests with a shared prefix can reuse its KV on the decode worker instead of allocating and transferring another copy for every request.

This relieves decode KV capacity pressure and allows more requests to generate concurrently. Recurrent state remains request-local: each request uses the full-prompt state received from prefill, preserving correctness for requests with different suffixes.

## Modifications

- Decouple prefix KV matching from Mamba/KDA checkpoints

items.body:
`experimental_fn` / `experimental_cls` decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the *minor* component of the version:

```python
PkgVersion(introduced_with_version).minor + max_lifetime < PkgVersion(mcore_version).minor
```

Once mcore crosses a major boundary and the minor version resets to 0, this comparison can never fire again, so expired experimental APIs silently stop being flagged. MoRIIO READ pairs prefill and decode sliding-window blocks by clipping each block list from its end. - Also fixes the full-attention pairing when only the prefiller has a lookahe

items.author: aarnetalman
items.summary: Deterministic inference promises the same output for a request whatever else the server has served, but on hybrid sliding-window models (for example gpt-oss) the radix cache breaks that. The hybrid SWA memory pool keeps only the sliding window of KV for the sl…
items.body:
## Motivation

Deterministic inference promises the same output for a request whatever else the server has served, but on hybrid sliding-window models (for example gpt-oss) the radix cache breaks that. The hybrid SWA memory pool keeps only the sliding window of KV for the sliding-window layers and evicts the rest. A cached prefix can then be reused only as far as its sliding-window KV is still there, so how much of a prompt is served from the cache, and so how it is prefilled, depends on which earlier requests evicted what. The result of the same request changes with the server's history.

items.body:
## Motivation

Diffusion host-memory planning can overcommit pinned memory when a parent cgroup has a larger limit but less remaining headroom than the child. For example, a child using 10GiB of 32GiB under a parent using 60GiB of 64GiB has 4GiB remaining, not 22GiB. Sibling usage counts against the parent.

## Modifications

Select the ancestor with the least `max(0, limit - usage)` rather than the least numeric limit. Apply the existing file-cache exclusion before comparison. Extend the existing budget tests with four v1/v2 cases, including cache-adjusted headroom.

items.title: [Kernel] Use 16-row tiles for SM89 int8 CUTLASS GEMM at M in (16, 64] for small N
items.author: amankarki151
items.summary: On SM89 (Ada), the int8 W8A8 CUTLASS GEMM gets ~1.5x slower when M goes from 16 to 17, and again from 32 to 33. The dispatch moves from 16-row tiles to 32-row tiles at M=17 and 64-row tiles at M=33. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #56924. On SM89 (Ada), the int8 W8A8 CUTLASS GEMM gets ~1.5x slower when M goes from 16 to 17, and again from 32 to 33. The dispatch moves from 16-row tiles (`sm89_int8_config_M16`) to 32-row tiles at M=17 and 64-row tiles at M=33. For the small-N layers of models like Qwen3-1.7B (N=2048, K=2048) that halves or quarters the number of CTAs (32 CTAs with 32x64 tiles on a 128-SM RTX 4090), so most of the GPU sits idle and each CTA does more work.

This PR keeps the existing `sm89_int8_config_M16` config for M in (16, 32] when N <= 4096 and for M in (32, 64] when N <= 2048. No

items.title: [Perf][Attention] 16-byte-align per-token-head KV slots so Triton vectorizes loads
items.author: noon-at-cgn
items.summary: Pads KV cache slot strides to 16-byte alignment so Triton vectorizes int8/fp8 K/V loads, eliminating byte-at-a-time accesses and achieving 1.25–1.96× kernel speedup with up to 21% TTFT reduction.
items.body:
## Overview

TRITON_ATTN packs int8/fp8 per-token-head KV as `[K | k_scale | V | v_scale]`. The slot stride (520 B at head_size 256, 264 B at 128) and the V offset (+260/+132 B) are not multiples of 16, so `kernel_unified_attention` loads K/V one byte at a time. This PR pads each K/V half to 16 bytes. Related: #56081, #56164, #61925.

AI assistance was used: an AI coding agent wrote the code and tests under my direction, drafted this description, and automated the test and benchmark runs; I chose the approach and reviewed every changed line and the results.

items.author: yijingl-nvidia
items.summary: TRTLLM has a config option, checkpoint IO policy, to set what weight loading method to load checkpoint weights. Previously this option is type, this PR changes it to its own enum.
items.body:
## Description

TRTLLM has a config option, checkpoint IO policy, to set what weight loading method to load checkpoint weights.
Previously this option is `str` type, this PR changes it to its own enum `CheckpointIOPolicy`.

Benefits:
- Functions using the option becomes easier to understand as its input/output now has type `CheckpointIOPolicy` instead of a `str`

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Fixes gc-threshold and freeze_gc not propagating to scheduler, detokenizer, and multi-tokenizer workers, causing unoptimized GC across server subprocesses.

`--gc-threshold` is applied with `gc.set_threshold` in the launching process only. items.body:
When a Mistral model streams a tool call in the compact format (`[TOOL_CALLS]name[ARGS]{...}`, used by the newer Mistral, Magistral and Devstral templates), `MistralDetector.parse_streaming_increment` calls `_try_parse_compact_args_format` on every delta, and `_extract_json_value` walks the whole arguments buffer character by character in Python to see whether the JSON value has closed yet. The work per delta grows with the arguments already received, so a long call is quadratic: streaming 34 KB of arguments in 4 character deltas takes about 2.6 s of parser CPU on the event loop.

items.author: moraxu
items.summary: Fixes a server crash under speculative decoding with xgrammar guided decoding, and follows up on #20463. gives xgrammar the padded size, and xgrammar's lists the extra ids as special tokens but keeps no decoded string for them.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

Fixes a server crash under speculative decoding with xgrammar guided decoding, and follows up on #20463.

**Crash.** Models pad the LM head past the tokenizer's vocabulary; Muse Spark Open has 201,818 tokens and 202,048 LM-head rows. `XGrammarMatcherFactory` gives xgrammar the padded size, and xgrammar's `TokenizerInfo` lists the extra ids as special tokens but keeps no decoded string for them. Asked to accept one, xgrammar before 0.2.6 (TRT-LLM pins 0.1.32) rejects it, but first prints its decoded string: an out-of-bounds read that segfaults the process.

items.body:
Fixes #20485

## Description

This PR fixes two logic defects in `NGramPoolManager.get_draft_tokens`:

1. **Candidate pruning:** Removing elements from an `OrderedSet` while iterating over it can skip candidates, leaving shorter matches in the pool. Iterating over a snapshot (`list(pool[pattern])`) ensures all shorter matches are considered for removal.
2. **Single-match invariant:** When `is_keep_all=False`, the existing update branch can allow additional matches to be added to the pool. Guarding that branch with `self.is_keep_all` preserves the single-match behavior.

## Summary

KV cache manager V2 objects can be destroyed on a Python thread that has no current CUDA context. Their teardown then fails with `CUDA driver error: 201 (invalid device context)` and poisons KVCM2 for the rest of the process. This PR binds each object's CUDA context for its teardown.

items.body:
## Description

The merge queue runs L0_MergeRequest.groovy on a commit that has no GitHub PR and no GitLab MR. Today such a build falls into the GitLab MR branch of the changed-file code, calls `projects/null/merge_requests/null/diffs`, fails to parse the 404 reply, and goes on with an empty changed file list. So CBTS, auto trigger tags, the multi-GPU check and the waive list merge all run without knowing what changed.

This PR adds an optional `base_commit` field to `gitlabTriggerPhrase`. The merge queue wrapper sets it to the merge base of the queue commit and `main`.

items.author: svcnemo-autobot
items.summary: Fixes disaggregated serving where imported decode requests with long prompts incorrectly fail max_tokens check despite having an existing KV cache.
items.body:
## Background

In disaggregated serving, `_finalize_kv_handoff_import()` admits an imported decode request through `add_request()`. Unless chunked prefill was enabled, `_add_request()` failed any prompt longer than `context.max_tokens` with `TokenOverflowError`. That limit bounds how much prefill work one step does. An imported prompt's KV cache already exists and the request goes straight to decode, so a long disaggregated prompt failed on the decode engine.

## What changed

- `dynamic_engine.py`: `add_request()` and `_add_request()` take a keyword-only `prompt_is_prefilled: bool = False`. `

Decode engines in disaggregated serving admit prefilled requests through `add_request_with_kv_handoff()`. The inference review found two gaps:

- Unlike `SUBMIT_REQUEST`, the `SUBMIT_REQUEST_WITH_KV` handler in `schedule_requests()` had no `try/except`. That error, or any other handoff validation error, escaped the loop and the client never got a reply.

## Background

PyExecutor._executor_loop_overlap single-thread 1-step lookahead scheduler 在高并发 decode 场景下，per-iter host 开销与 GPU 开销相当，导致 GPU 空转 ~580µs/iter。

## Problem

Single-threaded executor loop cannot overlap host scheduling + dispatch with GPU forward.

## Solution

Opt-in 2-batch pipelined executor loop (enable_pipelined_scheduler):

1. ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) 专属 worker 线程跑 forward+sample dispatch
2. 主线程同时 schedule 下一批 + drain 最老批结果
3. CUDA event-based cross-thread synchronization
4. 严格线程隔离：scheduling collectives 仅在主线程执行

# What does this PR do?

### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

The problem: MiniMax-M3's decode index scorer (`minimax_m3_index_decode_score`, CuTe DSL) reads each shared-memory stage with `ldmatrix`. items.title: Fix FP8/FP4 context loss during GDN and KDA recompute
items.author: QiZhangNV
items.summary: When selective recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward.
items.body:
When selective `gdn` recomputate is enabled with FP8/FP4, checkpoint replay loses TE's quantization context. Projection GEMMs fall back to BF16 during recomputation and backward. With MXFP8 parameter gathering enabled, this can also cause a missing `main_grad` error.

Use `te_checkpoint` for FP8/FP4 in GDN and KDA to preserve the quantization context, keeping the existing checkpoint path for non-quantized configurations.

Validated with 12 GPU regression cases and a single-node, four-GPU Qwen-style proxy covering MXFP8, NVFP4, and MXFP8 parameter gathering.

items.title: [data] fix: re-raise ImportError in overlong prompt filter instead of dropping all rows
items.author: yweiii
items.summary: When an optional dependency is missing (for example for multimodal data), raises inside for every sample. The catch-all in, added in #3814 to drop malformed rows, swallows it and returns, so the filter silently drops the whole dataset.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When an optional dependency is missing (for example `qwen_vl_utils` for multimodal data), `_process_multi_modal_info` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` inside `doc2len` for every sample. The catch-all `except Exception` in `maybe_filter_out_long_prompts`, added in #3814 to drop malformed rows, swallows it and returns `max_prompt_length + 1`, so the filter silently drops the whole dataset. items.title: Accumulate the embedding weight gradient into main_grad
items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: With gradientaccumulationfusion, VocabParallelEmbedding's backward now adds its weight gradient into maingrad itself, as the linear layers do, and hands autograd a ZeroTensor, so the DDP hook still runs but adds nothing. PyTorch's embedding backward builds a d…
items.body:
With gradient_accumulation_fusion, VocabParallelEmbedding's backward now adds its weight gradient into main_grad itself, as the linear layers do, and hands autograd a ZeroTensor, so the DDP hook still runs but adds nothing. PyTorch's embedding backward builds a dense [vocab, hidden] gradient that the hook then adds whole, about 1 ms per embedding use for a 129280 x 7168 vocabulary on VR200.

For 3073 to 8192 tokens, Triton kernels add only the rows of the tokens that occur, with the arithmetic of PyTorch's sort-based embedding backward followed by main_grad.add_, so main_grad is bit-identical.

items.author: sraman-rgb
items.summary: Optimizes MLA query RoPE forward kernel by replacing two stride-2 loads/stores with contiguous memory access, reducing kernel time from 18.7μs to 11.3μs on VR200.
items.body:
The in-place query RoPE forward (_mla_rope_fwd_inplace_kernel) read the emb_dim RoPE elements of every head with two stride-2 loads, one for the even and one for the odd elements, and with remove_interleaving it wrote them back with two stride-2 stores. It now loads them with one contiguous load and splits the even and odd elements in registers, and writes the remove_interleaving output with one contiguous store. For DeepSeek-V3's query, [4096, 1, 128, 192] in bf16, the kernel takes 11.3 us instead of 18.7 us on VR200.

items.title: fix: Defer frozen MFSDP cleanup without input gradients
items.author: wujingyue
items.summary: An MFSDP unit owning only frozen weights can still contain a separately sharded trainable child. If the unit's inputs do not require gradients, PyTorch fires its full backward hook when output gradients arrive.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

An MFSDP unit owning only frozen weights can still contain a separately sharded trainable child. If the unit's inputs do not require gradients, PyTorch fires its full backward hook when output gradients arrive. Resharding there frees frozen weights before internal backward consumes them to compute the child's gradients.

For ordinary backward, defer that unit's completion callback until the final autograd callback. Weight cleanup runs after every microbatch; automatic gradient synchronization run

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

With a vLLM rollout replica that has `data_parallel_size > 1` (e.g. DP + EP inside one server), each DP engine has its own prefix cache. `LLMServerClient` sends every turn under a fresh uuid and no DP rank, so vLLM's internal DP load balancer picks the least-loaded engine per request, and the turns of a multi-turn session land on different DP ranks and miss their prefix cache.

`LLMServerClient` now forwards the sticky caller id as `session_id`. `vLLMHttpServer` turns it into `data_parallel_rank = crc32(session_id) % data_parallel_size` using its own DP size and pass

items.author: ZhiliangWu
items.summary: Fix when in the fully async trainer. With offload on, the local shards are already on CPU, so returns a tensor that shares memory with the live shard, not a copy.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fix `fsdp2_sharded_save_to_cpu` when `param_offload=True` in the fully async trainer.

With offload on, the local shards are already on CPU, so `.detach().cpu()` returns a tensor that shares memory with the live shard, not a copy. In `FullyAsyncTrainer._compute_old_log_prob`, `restore_model_from_cpu(1)` then also overwrites the snapshot from `save_model_to_cpu(k)`, and `restore_model_from_cpu(k)` brings back the weights from the start of the sync window instead of the current ones. As a result, every local step trains again from the weights at the start of the window

## 背景

此 PR 添加了一个**跨仓库自动文档翻译工作流**（`schedule_doc_translate_ascend.yaml`），它能自动将 `docs/ascend_tutorial/zh/` 下的中文文档翻译为 `docs/ascend_tutorial/en/` 下的英文文档，并按周计划执行。


## 工作原理

此工作流在 `verl-project/verl` 仓库中运行，并使用**独立的私有 Fork 仓库**来存储翻译工具（Python 翻译引擎、技能/提示文档以及 `.po` 翻译记忆库）。这使得上游仓库保持整洁——它仅接收 `en/` 文档和工作流文件的更改。

**工作流步骤：**

1. **检出（Checkout）** Fork 私有仓库的 `main` 分支（包含 `translate_md.py`、`skill.md`、`.po` 缓存）。
2. **同步（Sync）** Fork 的 `main` 分支与最新的上游 `main` 分支（通过 `git merge`），然后将同步后的 `main` 分支推送回 Fork。
3. **翻译（Translate）** — 运行 `translate_md.py`，将每个中文文档拆分为块，复用 `.po` 文件中的缓存翻译，仅对更改/未翻译的块调用 OpenAI 兼容的

`ToolAgentLoop._call_tool` runs `create`, `execute` and `release` for every tool call. ### What does this PR do?

Cancelling `LLMServerClient.generate()` while the router has allocated a server but has not returned the RPC result leaks the in-flight count: acquisition happens before the generation `try/finally`. The FP8 end-to-end section of `docs/low_precision/fp8.md` lists `NVTE_FP8_BLOCK_SCALING_FP32_SCALES=1` as a general requirement. It only applies on Hopper.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

items.author: yuyz-cyber

items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Problem

items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.
items.body:
## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

- Reuse the existing `_wrap_ipv6` helpe

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

items.body:
`abort()` ordered the worker calls as pause → drain → resume, which can hang the rollout under `--partial-rollout` with continuously-submitting (e.g. multi-turn) rollouts.

The call to `/pause?mode=abort` aborts the known requests but leaves the engine in`PAUSED_NEW` status, so a `/generate` POST that races in after the pause ends up in the waiting queue and never returns. One such request blocks the `while state.pendings` drain forever - and `/resume`, the only thing that frees it, sat after the drain.

Fixes #274

## Summary

On Ascend NPU, the default `--megatron-to-hf-mode raw` causes abnormally high `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` (0.05–0.18 vs GPU ~0.025) and prevents GRPO from converging (`pg_loss` / `pg_clipfrac` stay at 0).

This PR defaults to `bridge` when `is_npu()` is true, so NPU users do not need to pass `--megatron-to-hf-mode bridge` explicitly. GPU behavior is unchanged (`raw`).
